title: Assess major cardiovascular risk factors for hypertension
recommended_action: Measure systolic and diastolic blood pressure, assess tobacco use, obtain lipid profile (total cholesterol, LDL, HDL), screen for diabetes mellitus, record age, obtain family history of premature cardiovascular disease, and measure waist circumference

evidence.passage: Table 4: Major risk factors for cardiovascular diseases    Levels of SBP and DBP   Tobacco use    Dyslipidemia  o  Total cholesterol >5.1 mmol/L  o  LDL >3 mmol/l, OR  o  HDL <1 (men) and <1.2 mmol/l (women)    Diabetes mellitus   Age (>55 years for men, >65 years for women)    Family history of premature cardiovascular diseases  o  (men <55 years or women <65 years)    Central obesity  o  (Waist circumference >90 cm for men, >80 cm for women)

title: Screen for hypertension mediated organ damage (HMOD)
recommended_action: Perform clinical examination and appropriate tests to identify organ damage: cardiac exam for LVH signs, ECG/echo; neurological exam for TIA/stroke signs; peripheral pulse exam; renal function tests (GFR, proteinuria, microalbuminuria); fundoscopic exam for retinopathy

title: Referral indications for hypertension
recommended_action: Refer to appropriate specialist when any indication present

evidence.passage: Patients with the following conditions should be referred to the appropriate specialist for further assessment. Indications for referral to the appropriate specialist include: accelerated or malignant hypertension; suspected secondary hypertension; resistant hypertension; recent onset of target organ damage; pregnancy; children <18 years old.
